title: Over or Under the Muscle? Breast Implant Placement Compared
meta_description: Under the muscle: less visible, less contracture, may hurt more early. Over: recovery may be shorter, implant should stay put when you flex.
excerpt: Where the implant sits changes how it looks, how your first weeks feel and what happens when you flex. Here is what each placement trades, what the evidence does and does not show, and the questions that settle it at your consultation.
quick_answer:
Are breast implants better over or under the muscle?

Neither suits everyone. Sientra's and Allergan's labeling say implants under the muscle are harder to see or feel and carry less capsular contracture, but surgery may be longer and more painful, and The Aesthetic Society says they may move when you flex. Over the muscle, recovery may be shorter, but implants show more.

images.alt: A comparison card titled Over or Under the Muscle: The Trade-offs. Under the muscle: less visible and harder to feel, capsular contracture through 10 years 15.7%, recovery may be longer and more painful, implant may move when you flex, easier mammogram views. Over the muscle: more visible and easier to feel, capsular contracture through 10 years 26.3%, recovery may be shorter and less painful, implant should stay in place, harder mammogram views. The footer credits Allergan's 10-year study (Spear and Murphy, 2014) for the contracture rates.
